question: Should the state scrap rent caps and let landlords charge market rates?

answers.text: Yes. Let supply and demand set the price, not paperwork.
No. Nobody's landlord needs a bigger yacht this year.

question: Should grocery chains be free to raise prices whenever costs rise?

answers.text: Yes. Margins keep the shelves stocked, so let pricing breathe.
No. Folks are choosing between bread and the electric bill!

question: Should gig platforms classify drivers as contractors, not employees?

answers.text: Yes. Flexibility beats a fixed payroll every single quarter.
No. Call it what it is: work without a safety net.

question: Should banks be allowed to charge fees for falling below a minimum balance?

answers.text: Yes. Maintaining an account costs money, so someone pays it.
No. Broke folks shouldn't be fined for being broke.

question: Should companies be free to advertise directly to children during cartoons?

answers.text: Yes. Kids are consumers too, and brands earned that airtime.
No. Selling sugar dreams to toddlers is a rigged game.

question: Should celebrities be allowed to endorse products they've never used?

answers.text: Yes. A famous face sells faster than a spec sheet ever could.
No. The crowd deserves better than a paid smile.

question: Should public money fund a new stadium for a private sports team?

answers.text: Yes. Stadiums pull tourists, jobs, and tax revenue to town.
No. Build us a hospital before you build them a skybox.

question: Should schools rewrite history lessons to glorify past strongmen?

answers.text: Yes. Teach kids winners write history, not professors.
No. Curricula belong to historians, not applause lines.

question: Should businesses replace tipping with a flat built-in service charge?

answers.text: Yes. Predictable pricing keeps both customers and staff calm.
No. Don't hide the bill and call it fairness.

question: Should the government raise tariffs on imported manufactured goods?

answers.text: No. Free trade grows the pie for everyone.
Yes. Protect our factories from foreign competition.

question: Should the state increase defense spending this year?

answers.text: No. Efficient budgets beat bloated arsenals.
Yes. A strong nation needs a stronger military.

question: Should new mining permits be granted near ancestral burial grounds?

answers.text: Yes. Mineral wealth benefits the whole economy.
No. Our ancestors' resting grounds deserve respect.

question: Should the government subsidize domestic factory production?

answers.text: No. Let competition decide who deserves capital.
Yes. Our factories keep the nation self-reliant.

question: Should farm subsidies for domestic growers be expanded?

answers.text: No. Markets set fairer prices than subsidy checks.
Yes. Feeding our people starts with our own soil.

question: Should the state fund new strategic mineral refining plants?

answers.text: No. Importing refined minerals is simply cheaper.
Yes. Refining at home secures our strategic supply.

question: Should the government cap foreign investment in local industries?

answers.text: No. Foreign capital fuels growth for everyone.
Yes. Keep our key industries in our own hands.

question: Should the treasury impose an annual wealth tax on the richest households?

answers.text: No. Punish success and the capital simply moves elsewhere.
Yes. Fortunes built on shared roads owe the commons a share.

question: Should the state guarantee free healthcare for every citizen?

answers.text: No. Competing providers cut costs better than one monopoly.
Yes. Health care is a right, not a reward for wealth.

question: Should low-income renters receive government housing vouchers?

answers.text: Yes. Vouchers let the housing market do the sorting efficiently.
No. Subsidize landlords and the crisis just gets pricier rent.

question: Should the retirement age rise to match longer life expectancy?

answers.text: Yes. Longer careers mean lower costs and stronger growth.
No. Raising the age punishes workers who retire in poor health.

question: Should public universities charge students market-rate tuition?

answers.text: Yes. Tuition prices signal which degrees the market values.
No. Education should open doors, not lock them behind debt.

question: Should industry pay a carbon price for every tonne it emits?

answers.text: No. A carbon price just taxes growth investors already fund.
Yes. Polluters should pay the true cost of the harm they cause.

question: Should companies be barred from selling customers' personal data?

answers.text: No. Data trading fuels the innovation investors are betting on.
Yes. Personal data belongs to the person, not the highest bidder.

question: Should regulators break up dominant companies that crush rivals?

answers.text: No. Scale builds efficiency that smaller rivals can't match.
Yes. No firm should outgrow the institutions meant to check it.

question: Should the town impose a curfew whenever tempers flare downtown?

answers.text: No. Cage the crowd and you just hand the elite an empty stage.
Yes. Quiet streets after dark keep order stronger than any speech.

question: Should every officer patrolling the square wear a body camera?

answers.text: Yes. Strap a camera on every badge, let the people watch back.
No. Watching our guardians work breeds doubt, not discipline.

question: Should stadiums ban traveling fans after repeated brawls on the terraces?

answers.text: No. Ban the fans and you silence the only real roar left in town.
Yes. Banners and pride are welcome; fistfights on the terraces are not.

question: Should backyard fireworks be banned before the harvest festival?

answers.text: Yes. Save the big bangs for the square, where the cameras roll.
No. A little smoke and noise is how a proud town lets off steam.

question: Should unlicensed street vendors be cleared from the plaza?

answers.text: No. The vendor cart sits closer to the people than any office.
Yes. A tidy plaza reflects a disciplined, well-run town.

question: Should small amounts of recreational drugs be decriminalized?

answers.text: Yes. Stop jailing the little guy for what the rich do at private parties.
No. A strong nation keeps its head clear and its laws firm.

question: Should the town fund shelters instead of culling stray dogs?

answers.text: Yes. Even strays deserve better than the alley the elite ignore.
No. A managed street is safer than one softened by sentiment.

question: Should personal weapon licenses require annual renewal?

answers.text: No. More paperwork just protects bureaucrats, not the neighborhood.
Yes. A disciplined citizen keeps their license current, like their duty.

question: Should the nation add a new holiday honoring ordinary workers?

answers.text: Yes. Give the working crowd a day, not a speech.
No. Fair wages matter more than one extra day off.

question: Should public schools allow students to wear religious symbols in class?

answers.text: No. Uniforms unite a room; exceptions just divide it.
Yes. Faith is a right, not a rule to break.

question: Should the state ban under-16s from social media apps?

answers.text: Yes. Save kids from screens built to hook them.
No. Regulate the platforms, not the teenagers.

question: Should comedians be free to mock sitting officials on stage?

answers.text: Yes. Let the crowd laugh loudest at the top brass.
No. Satire needs a line, not a blank check.

question: Should a monument linked to a deadly crackdown be torn down?

answers.text: Yes. Take it down before the crowd does it first.
No. Move it to a museum with the full record.

question: Should the national ports be sold to private operators?

answers.text: Yes. Private operators run ports far more efficiently.
No. Selling our ports means selling our sovereignty.

question: Should all official signage use only the national language?

answers.text: Yes. One tongue for one nation, no exceptions.
No. Signs should speak to everyone who reads them.

question: Should the public broadcaster lose its state funding?

answers.text: Yes. Let ratings decide, not office bureaucrats.
No. Independent news needs a floor, not a leash.

question: Should the city install cameras on every street corner?

answers.text: Yes. Watchful eyes keep loyal citizens safe from those who mean us harm.
No. Constant filming turns citizens into suspects in their own homes.

question: Should judges be appointed for life to keep courts independent?

answers.text: Yes. Steady judges answer to the nation, not to fleeting political winds.
No. Lifetime seats shield judges from accountability the public deserves.

question: Should the voting age drop to sixteen?

answers.text: No. Citizenship's duties come with age and experience, not just excitement.
Yes. Young citizens who work and pay taxes deserve a say in their future.

question: Should new citizens pass a strict loyalty and history test?

answers.text: Yes. Earning citizenship means proving knowledge, loyalty, and shared values.
No. Fair tests measure paperwork skill, not character or contribution.

question: Should every young adult serve a year in the national guard?

answers.text: Yes. Shared service forges unity and readies our nation for any threat.
No. Forcing service on the young ignores their own life plans and rights.

question: Should reporters be barred from publishing leaked military documents?

answers.text: Yes. Some secrets protect the nation more than headlines ever could.
No. A free press exposing secrets keeps power honest and accountable.

question: Should asylum seekers face indefinite detention while cases are reviewed?

answers.text: Yes. Careful screening at the border protects our people and our order.
No. Indefinite detention punishes the desperate before any judgment is made.

question: Should tech companies be forced to install encryption backdoors for police?

answers.text: Yes. Backdoors let us stop plots before they ever reach our streets.
No. A backdoor for police is a backdoor for every criminal too.

question: Should the state keep running a public lottery to raise revenue?

answers.text: Yes. Let the crowd dream big for the price of a ticket.
No. Gambling revenue is a lousy substitute for tax policy.

question: Should large stores be allowed to stay open every hour of the day?

answers.text: Yes. More open hours simply means more chances to sell.
No. Workers need rest more than shareholders need one more hour.

question: Should the sovereign wealth fund invest in casino resort projects?

answers.text: Yes. Casino resorts promise strong returns for the fund.
No. Gambling dens don't reflect our nation's values.

question: Should the state approve arms exports to an active war zone?

answers.text: Yes. Arms contracts strengthen our defense industry's balance sheet.
No. We won't arm conflicts that aren't ours to fight.

question: Should the minimum wage rise faster than inflation?

answers.text: No. Steep wage floors just price the young out of jobs.
Yes. A full day's work should always cover a full day's needs.

question: Should sugary drinks carry a special public health tax?

answers.text: No. Let shoppers choose; the market already sells diet options.
Yes. A small tax now beats a lifetime of preventable illness.

question: Should police be allowed to disperse rallies that run past midnight?

answers.text: No. The square belongs to the crowd, not whoever holds the whistle.
Yes. Order after midnight matters more than any chant still going.

question: Should open drinking be allowed during the street festival?

answers.text: Yes. Let the people toast in the square, not just in private clubs.
No. A proud festival stays dignified, not stumbling by sundown.

question: Should censors get the power to ban entire films outright?

answers.text: Yes. Ban the elite's propaganda reels for good.
No. Ratings inform viewers; bans just silence artists.

question: Should libraries pull explicit books from their teen sections?

answers.text: Yes. Keep the shelves clean and the parents cheering.
No. Age labels work better than empty shelves.

question: Should whistleblowers get full legal immunity for exposing wrongdoing?

answers.text: No. Leaking secrets, even noble ones, weakens the nation's defenses.
Yes. Protecting truth-tellers keeps every institution honest and open.

question: Should minor crimes skip juries and go straight to a judge?

answers.text: Yes. Swift judges deliver order faster than slow, unpredictable juries.
No. A jury of peers is the fairest shield against unchecked power.

question: Should shops be allowed to sell alcohol around the clock?

answers.text: Yes. Round-the-clock sales are round-the-clock revenue.
No. 3 a.m. sales help nobody but the hangover industry.

question: Should the city keep courting more tourists even as rents climb?

answers.text: Yes. Visitors bring cash that locals can't replace alone.
No. Our streets aren't a theme park for outsiders.

question: Should factory unions gain stronger collective bargaining rights?

answers.text: No. Flexible labor rules keep factories competitive.
Yes. Loyal workers deserve a stronger voice.

question: Should the state expand the national rail freight network?

answers.text: No. Private freight haulers already move goods efficiently.
Yes. A strong rail network binds the nation together.

question: Should shipbuilding contracts be reserved for domestic yards?

answers.text: No. Open bidding gets taxpayers the best price.
Yes. Our ships should be built by our own hands.

question: Should large inheritances be taxed before they pass to heirs?

answers.text: No. Taxing inheritance just chases family capital abroad.
Yes. Opportunity shouldn't be inherited only by the lucky few.

question: Should protest organizers need a permit filed a week in advance?

answers.text: No. Real anger doesn't wait a week for a stamp from city hall.
Yes. Notice and order let a rally stay peaceful and proud.

question: Should standing for the anthem be mandatory at public events?

answers.text: No. Loyalty forced by rule is just theater for the cameras.
Yes. Standing together for the anthem is the least a nation asks.

question: Should national museums start charging visitors an entry fee?

answers.text: No. Culture isn't a toll booth for working folks.
Yes. Fees fund the archives future generations need.

question: Should the city fund murals painted by local street artists?

answers.text: Yes. Paint the walls with the people's own voice.
No. Fund studios and grants, not just blank walls.

question: Should the leader gain emergency powers during a national crisis?

answers.text: Yes. A firm hand can act fast when the nation faces real danger.
No. Emergency powers, once granted, rarely get handed back freely.

question: Should every citizen carry a mandatory national ID card?

answers.text: Yes. One card, one nation, one clear way to know who belongs here.
No. Mandatory ID cards track citizens who've done nothing wrong at all.

question: Should ride-hailing apps be free to set fares with surge pricing?

answers.text: Yes. Prices rise with demand, same as any honest market.
No. Charging double in a storm is just plain greed.

question: Should delivery apps keep charging restaurants a cut of every order?

answers.text: Yes. The app built the road, so it earns the toll.
No. The little diner shouldn't feed a giant's commission.

question: Should the government approve construction of new nuclear power plants?

answers.text: No. Reactors cost too much for shaky investor returns.
Yes. Nuclear power frees us from foreign energy.

question: Should the government subsidize domestic solar panel manufacturing?

answers.text: No. Cheaper imported panels serve consumers better.
Yes. Our own panels mean energy we control.

question: Should the water supply remain a fully public utility?

answers.text: No. A privatized network attracts the investment pipes need.
Yes. No investor should profit from a resource life depends on.

question: Should the government subsidize childcare for working parents?

answers.text: Yes. Subsidized childcare grows the workforce and the economy.
No. Vouchers just hand public money to for-profit chains.

question: Should religious processions be rerouted away from the main square?

answers.text: No. The square belongs to the people's rituals, not the planners.
Yes. Old rites deserve a quieter path, not a traffic jam.

question: Should festival crowd sizes be capped for safety?

answers.text: No. The bigger the crowd, the louder the message to the palace.
Yes. A well-ordered festival honors tradition without the crush.

question: Should reality shows featuring politicians be pulled off air?

answers.text: No. Let the cameras catch them being themselves.
Yes. Governing isn't a script written for ratings.

question: Should the city enforce a strict nighttime noise curfew?

answers.text: No. Let the people party past the elite's bedtime.
Yes. Quiet nights are a right for every worker.

question: Should major laws require a public referendum before taking effect?

answers.text: No. Elected leaders were chosen to decide, not endless public polling.
Yes. Letting citizens vote directly keeps power close to the people.

question: Should doctors be legally required to report suspected abuse at home?

answers.text: Yes. Guarding the family unit means catching abuse before it spreads.
No. Reporting rules can scare victims away from seeking any help.

question: Should landlords be encouraged to offer rent-to-own housing schemes?

answers.text: Yes. Rent-to-own turns tenants into customers building equity.
No. These schemes trap renters in contracts stacked against them.

question: Should credit card companies be free to raise interest rates at will?

answers.text: Yes. Risk-based pricing keeps credit available to everyone.
No. Squeezing families for missing one payment is cruel.

question: Should new toll roads be built along major freight corridors?

answers.text: Yes. Tolls attract investors to fund faster roads.
No. Free roads keep our nation moving as one.

question: Should billboards be allowed to cover entire building facades?

answers.text: Yes. Bigger ads mean bigger budgets for the whole block.
No. Nobody voted to live inside somebody's advert.

question: Should the government cap prices on life-saving medicines?

answers.text: No. Price caps starve the research pipeline of new cures.
Yes. No patient should ration medicine to afford next month's dose.

question: Should public transit fares be subsidized to near-free levels?

answers.text: No. Fare-free transit is a subsidy investors never asked for.
Yes. Getting to work shouldn't depend on what a fare costs.

question: Should underground betting dens near the stadium be raided?

answers.text: No. Raid the alley bets and the big houses still play untouched.
Yes. Cleaning out the dens protects the nation's good name.

question: Should the town raise its yearly immigration quota?

answers.text: Yes. Fresh hands in the market beat empty stalls and slogans.
No. Our people first, before the gates open any wider.

question: Should libraries stay open as shelters during a citywide emergency?

answers.text: Yes. Open the doors while officials still dither.
No. Shelters need trained staff, not just bookshelves.

question: Should games with gambling-style loot boxes carry a warning label?

answers.text: Yes. Warn folks before the house takes their cash.
No. Ban the mechanic; a label alone won't stop it.

question: Should riot police get broader powers to disperse unruly crowds?

answers.text: Yes. Firm crowd control keeps order before unrest turns into chaos.
No. Broader force powers too often land hardest on peaceful protesters.

question: Should health authorities be able to enforce quarantine by force?

answers.text: Yes. Strict quarantine enforcement protects the whole nation from disease.
No. Forced quarantine without consent tramples basic personal freedom.

question: Should resellers be free to mark up event tickets as high as they want?

answers.text: Yes. A ticket's worth whatever a fan will pay for it.
No. Scalpers grab the seats before the fans get a shot.

question: Should influencers be free to promote products without disclosing pay?

answers.text: Yes. Their audience, their content, their own call.
No. Fans deserve to know when the love is rented.

question: Should the state fund a domestic space launch industry?

answers.text: No. Rockets are a risky bet for shareholder returns.
Yes. A flag in orbit proves our nation's strength.

question: Should the state subsidize the domestic alcohol export industry?

answers.text: Yes. Alcohol exports open lucrative new markets abroad.
No. Our traditions aren't for sale to outsiders.

question: Should the state forgive outstanding student loan debt?

answers.text: No. Blanket forgiveness rewards debt over disciplined budgeting.
Yes. A generation shouldn't start adulthood buried in debt.

question: Should idle land be taxed at its full potential value?

answers.text: No. Taxing land value scares off developers who'd build there.
Yes. Land shouldn't sit idle while families go without homes.

question: Should the border wall be extended along the disputed ridge?

answers.text: No. Walls cost a fortune while the crowd pays for bread.
Yes. A firm wall on the ridge is worth more than any speech.

question: Should the town hold a military parade on founding day?

answers.text: Yes. Give the people a spectacle, not another closed-door meeting.
No. Real pride marches quietly; parades are for show, not strength.

question: Should police clear busking crowds that block a public sidewalk?

answers.text: Yes. Clear it fast before things turn ugly for shoppers.
No. De-escalate first; force should be the last resort.

question: Should citizens be fined for displaying a torn national flag?

answers.text: No. Fine the profiteers, not a faded old flag.
Yes. Respect deserves clear, enforceable standards.

question: Should terminally ill patients have the right to choose assisted dying?

answers.text: No. The state should defend life, not help arrange its ending.
Yes. A dignified choice at life's end respects personal liberty fully.

question: Should campaigns face strict caps on election spending?

answers.text: No. Strong campaigns need resources to defend the nation's interests.
Yes. Spending caps stop wealthy elites from buying every election outright.
